head: 0fb4f68bc64dc4d5ea9d8f67b4c7c5cf65fa8ca8
title: Prevent half-precision distance-square overflow in contrastive losses
body:
## Change

Accumulate ContrastiveLoss and OnlineContrastiveLoss distance squares in at least float32, while preserving float64. The conversion happens after the configured distance function, so custom distance functions still receive their original embedding dtype. Online hard-pair selection uses the promoted distances as well.

An unnormalized float16 embedding can have a finite Euclidean distance whose square overflows. A distance near `362` is already sufficient. The positive term becomes infinity; multiplying that infinity by a zero negative-pair label can also produce NaN. The same finite inputs have a finite float32 objective and gradient.

This was reproduced with a locally constructed, trainable WordEmbeddings SentenceTransformer using the public loss forward/backward path. It is separate from #4020's hard-pair inclusion rule and #4078's batch-triplet distance implementation.

## Validation

[Exact-base CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43919834477) compares base `9ac7fdb4` and candidate `0fb4f68b` with PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**. In both environments the new tests produce **11 failures and 39 passes on unchanged base**; the candidate and existing contrastive tests produce **58 passes**. All pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The reference selects contributing pairs with Python numbers and differentiates their mathematical squared-distance objective in float64. Coverage includes four floating dtypes, ordinary and large distances, mixed labels, all-positive and all-negative batches, custom distances, and real encoder training with the built-in Euclidean metric. Tests check finite loss, finite gradients and agreement with the independent reference.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation and regression tests.
